findings.section: 10 10.2 (maintainer block, item h); the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing); plan (block O8)
findings.defect: Item h saves its answers 'under the entry of item g', but the note, now the one home of the entry, defines an entry as a heading 'followed by the three reads' and never mentions item h, so the required-name try has no slot, and with more than one entry 'the entry of item g' does not say which.
findings.scenario: The maintainer writes the narrowed entry at one sitting and runs item h at a later one; the note's format admits no fourth section, so the answers go in a new entry (which then needs a verdict heading and three reads) or are appended to an old one, and block O8's pass, which reads only the verdict, accepts the sitting with no record of which check the ruleset counts.
findings.change: The note gives the entry an optional fourth part, 'the required-name try of item h, when it ran', with its expected answers, and says item h's answers go in the first entry whose verdict is narrowed, or in a later entry headed by its own date; O8's pass names that part. Cost: two sentences in the note and a clause in O8.
findings.evidence: docs/spec/10-testing-style.md:924-925 'save the API answers under the entry of item g'; docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:123-124 'An entry is a heading `### <date>: narrowed` or `### <date>: not narrowed`, followed by the three reads'; docs/plan.md:221 Pass 'the entry's verdict is narrowed, read against the expected answers the note lists'.

findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing, read 2); 10 10.2 (item g)
findings.defect: Read 2 lists the keys of 'that socket' on the host, but nothing reads which socket the host forwards, and the GitHub account's SSH keys page that R15-04's Resolution named is gone, so a signing key that is also registered as an authentication key passes as 'the signing key'.
findings.scenario: The operator's signing key was added to GitHub both as a signing key and as an authentication key (GitHub allows the same key in both lists). The host forwards only that key, read 2 shows the signing key and no other, the entry reads narrowed, and the forwarded key can still push over SSH to every repository the account reaches; or the maintainer lists the host's own agent socket rather than the one the sbx setting forwards.
findings.change: Read 2 adds the two host reads R15-04 listed: the sbx setting or kit that names the forwarded socket, and the account's SSH keys page (authentication keys), checked that no forwarded key appears among the authentication keys. Cost: two lines in the note.
findings.evidence: docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:143-147 'the keys of the forwarded socket, listed by `ssh-add -l` on the host with `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` set to that socket. Expected: the signing key, and no GitHub authentication key'; docs/reviews/round-15.md R15-04 Resolution 'the forwarding configuration the host gives the sandbox (the sbx setting or kit that forwards the agent) and the GitHub account's SSH keys page, each against a known list'.

findings.section: plan (block O8); 10 10.2 (maintainer block, item a); index (S2)
findings.defect: Decision 1 of ADR 0011, removing the administrator role's bypass of the default-branch ruleset, on which S2's evidence waits, is in no block's 'What the maintainer does' and has no pass; it appears only in O8's Recommendation column, and its evidence home ('under Evidence') belongs to no pull request in O8.
findings.scenario: The maintainer runs O8 as its columns say, narrows the token and writes the entry, and skips the recommendation; the default-branch ruleset keeps its bypass actor through v1.0.0, so S2 stays at 'the run, not the ruleset, is the evidence' by omission, and no block's pass shows it.
findings.change: O8 (or its own block) lists decision 1 under 'What the maintainer does', with the pass 'the saved API answer shows the default-branch ruleset with no bypass actor' and where that answer is saved (the note's entry, as for items g and h, or a named pull request). Cost: one plan row edit, and one clause in 10 10.2 item a if the evidence home moves.

findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing)
findings.defect: The return rule is not testable as written: 'the rows it fired stay fired' has two possible referents for 'it', 'the token rows of the index and of 05 5.4' is not listed anywhere, and two entries with the same date have no order for 'first' and 'later'.
findings.scenario: A narrowed entry and a not narrowed entry are written on the same date after a re-read; a reader cannot tell which is later, so whether the token rows stand in the narrowed state is undecided, and 'it' read as the later entry suggests a not narrowed entry fires rows.
findings.change: 'the rows the event fired stay fired'; name the rows returned (the index token-narrowing row and the 05 5.4 token and approval-line rows); entries are in the order they appear in the note, newest last. Cost: one sentence.
findings.evidence: docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:128-131 'A later entry whose verdict is not narrowed returns the token rows of the index and of 05 5.4 to the state before the narrowing; the rows it fired stay fired'.

findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing, read 3); index (the token-narrowing row); plan (block O8)
findings.defect: 'A later read leaves it out' can mean a read made after release.yml exists or any read after the first, and if O8 slips past T088 the first entry also skips the tag try, so the index's 'not measured until that entry' would become never measured with no text saying so.
findings.scenario: O8 has no task waiting on it and is due before C7 only by recommendation; the maintainer narrows the token after T088 lands release.yml, the entry omits the tag try under the guard, and whether a fine-grained token passes the tag ruleset's bypass stays unmeasured into the release while the index row still promises the entry measures it.
findings.change: 'a read made once release.yml exists leaves it out and records the tag answer as not measured'; the index row says the tag answer is measured only by an entry made before release.yml lands. Cost: two clauses.
findings.evidence: docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:150-152 'The tag try runs only while no `release.yml` exists ...; a later read leaves it out'; docs/spec.md:348 'whether it can create a `v*` tag through the tag ruleset's bypass is not measured until that entry'; docs/plan.md:221 'none: no task waits on it ... it is due before checkpoint C7'.

lens_critique: Success read only through S1 to S11 under-weights process controls that no S row measures: the token narrowing and the bypass removal sit outside every success criterion except through S2's fallback wording, so a control reviewer can find them complete when they are only scheduled. Missing viewpoint, from the lens titles: the operator as the one human in the loop, whose sittings and attention are the scarce resource every maintainer block spends (L14 is on duty, not the person whose time the blocks budget).
